priceSnapshot.note: The day ends by giving back everything it made, and it did so through the most instructive event of the week. At 22:00Z - 17:00 Bogota - BTC broke out. The hourly bar opened at 65,200.5 and ran to 65,490.3, clearing the 65,388.0 high of 07 August and the 65,423.7 high of 31 July in a single move. That is the multi-week range top, untouched since July, taken out on the tape. It held for minutes. The same hourly bar closed at 65,077.4, 413 points off its high, and the following hour closed at 64,899.3 with a low of 64,838.7. Spot now reads 64,912.3, which is 578.0 points BELOW the high it printed two and a half hours ago and 302.6 points below the midday reference at 65,214.9, a fall of 0.464%. Against the 64,852.0 midnight stamp the entire day amounts to +60.3 points, +0.093%. A failed breakout above a multi-week range high is a materially different object from a range that simply held, and the desk is treating it as one.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $64,650 - held UNCHANGED for an ELEVENTH consecutive session, and for the first time in three sessions price is walking back toward it rather than away. Spot 64,912.3 leaves 262.3 points of clearance, 0.40%, which is 0.19 of a daily ATR and the tightest the line has been since 08 August. What still stands between price and the trigger has thinned to three levels from six: the session low at 64,838.7, the 1H EMA100 at 64,783.4, the $411,377 realized-liquidation shelf at 64,750 and the daily EMA50 at 64,683.1. The 15m EMA200 at 64,968.2 and the 1H EMA50 at 64,974.1 that were supports six hours ago are now overhead. The line stays where it is because it is still the correct structural break - a settled hourly close beneath 64,650 loses the daily EMA50 and ends the higher-low sequence that has run since 03:00Z - but the desk is no longer describing it as remote.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $65,300, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. Held UNCHANGED from the midday session because the trigger did its job and deserves to stay exactly where it is. Price traded to 65,490.3, a full 190 points through the level, and the trigger did NOT fire - because it never asked for a wick, it asked for a settled close, and the 22:00Z bar closed at 65,077.4. The open-interest half of the condition rejected the move independently: open interest FELL 1.66% across the window rather than rising. Both halves said no and both halves were right within the hour. This is the third consecutive test of the open-interest confirmation rule and the third time it has scored, so it is retained verbatim rather than adjusted.

decisionBox.changed: Position flips from ADD to REDUCE and the tilt flips from bullish to bearish - the first change of direction in four sessions, and it is driven by an event rather than by drift. The midday session was right that 65,300 was the honest next test and it was right to leave 7.38 USDT dry rather than deploy it all. What it could not know is that the test would be taken and failed inside a single hour. Four things flipped together with the price. Open interest FELL 1.66% to $2.0566B where the midday recorded it RISING 3.62%, so the breakout was covering rather than accumulation. The long/short account ratio ROSE from 1.13 to 1.22, its highest of the week, meaning the crowd that was fading the rally at midday has swung to chasing it - the long-crowding vulnerability the midday said had been removed is back and larger. The 1H MACD histogram collapsed from +41.03 to -13.60 and 1H RSI from 66.64 to 40.42. And a fresh $237,002 all-short liquidation band printed at 65,500, which is the tape's record of exactly how the breakout was manufactured. The reduce line and the add trigger are both untouched; what changed is which one the desk now expects to see first.

overnightRisk: The next report is at roughly 02:00 Bogota and the gap between now and then is the highest-risk window of the day for this book, for four specific and stackable reasons. FIRST, the immediate one: 64,750 sits 162.3 points below spot and it is the largest LONG-side liquidation shelf on the map, $267,210 of the $411,377 in that band, and the long/short account ratio at 1.22 says there are more longs positioned above it now than at any point this week. A failed breakout that leaves crowded longs above a long-liquidation shelf is the classic setup for an overnight flush, and the 64,650 reduce trigger sits only 100 points beneath that shelf. SECOND, macro reopened for the Asian week in the ninety minutes before this report and reopened against crypto: the dollar index is 99.65, up 0.111 or 0.11%, the US 10-year yield is 4.672%, up 1.4 basis points, and Brent is 84.49, up 1.13%. Higher dollar, higher yields and higher oil all at once is the least helpful combination for BTC, and none of it was in the price when the 22:00Z breakout was attempted. THIRD, Monday 10 August is the first spot-ETF creation session since the 07 August +101.7M print, and it lands during the overnight window rather than after it. The five-session streak of +865.3M decayed from 244.4 to 137.6 to 101.7 across its final three days; a first negative print into a failed breakout would confirm the decay and there is no way to hedge it from here. FOURTH, liquidity is at its thinnest of the week - Sunday night into Monday Asia, with the 15m ATR at 127.31 already elevated by the whipsaw, so a modest sell order travels much further than it would at midday. A resting stop is the only protection that works while nobody is watching, and it is recommended at 64,650: below the 64,750 shelf so a routine sweep of that magnet does not take the book out, and exactly on the invalidation the desk has defended for eleven sessions. The bull case for the gap is not empty - the 64,722.7 low has held for twenty-two hours and the daily EMA50 at 64,683.1 has not been closed beneath all week - but it is now the smaller half of the distribution.

liquidation.note: Still the largest band on the map and still spent. Bucketing all 377 fills returned by OKX /public/liquidation-orders over the 2026-08-09T01:33:22Z to 2026-08-10T00:11:08Z window into 250-USD bands - BTC-USDT-SWAP contract multiplier 0.01 BTC - the 65,250 band carries $794,154 of the $1,720,689 total across 156 fills, 46.2% of everything liquidated in 22 hours 38 minutes. The composition has grown even more one-sided since midday: $782,951 SHORT against $11,203 long, a 70:1 ratio where the midday recorded 39:1. It is deliberately flagged magnet FALSE, a downgrade from the midday's magnet TRUE, and that downgrade is the single most important edit in this report. Price went through this band, cleared 240 points above it, and came straight back. The shorts that were sitting here have been carried out and were not replaced; what is left is not a pool of fuel but the wreckage of one that already burned. Treating it as an upside magnet a second time would be reading the same signal twice.

A band that did not exist six hours ago and is the tape's exact receipt for how the breakout was made. $237,002 across 60 fills, ONE HUNDRED PERCENT short - not a single long fill printed here. This is the cohort that was positioned for the 65,388 to 65,423.7 range top to hold, and the 65,490.3 spike existed to take them out. The forced buying it produced is precisely why the move looked violent and precisely why it had nothing behind it: once those 60 fills cleared, the bid that had been manufacturing the rally stopped, and price fell 578 points in two and a half hours. Read alongside open interest FALLING 1.66% across the same window, this is a short squeeze that terminated rather than a breakout that began.

The shelf the midday session named as the place to buy a pullback, now 87.7 points ABOVE spot and converted from support into the first overhead obstacle. Its composition inverted in the process and that inversion is the warning. At midday it held $69,677 across 18 fills, $59,463 of it short. It now holds $278,155 across 30 fills, of which $227,782 is LONG against $50,374 short. Longs are being liquidated at 65,000, not shorts. The confluence that made it attractive six hours ago - the round number, the 15m EMA100 at 65,057.0, the 1H EMA20 at 65,065.8 - is still there, but it now sits above price and works as resistance. The midday's plan to deploy the last 7.38 USDT into a retest of this shelf is the plan this session is declining to execute.

The shelf that has defined the week, and for the first time in three sessions it is the nearest magnet and the one that matters. $411,377 across 131 fills, and the composition is the mirror image of everything above spot: $267,210 LONG against $144,167 short. It has grown $149,045 since the midday read, all of it long-side, which means longs have already been getting carried out here during today's chop. It sits 162.3 points below spot with the 1H EMA100 at 64,783.4 immediately above it and the 24-hour low at 64,722.7 immediately below, and the daily EMA50 at 64,683.1 and the 64,650 reduce trigger a further 40 to 100 points under that. This is where the overnight risk lives: a crowded long book at a 1.22 account ratio sitting directly above the largest long-liquidation shelf on the chart, into the thinnest liquidity window of the week.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull has flipped from up to DOWN and the flip is unusually clean, because every component of it moved the same way at the same time. The composition test: the two bands above spot are 97% and 100% short-side and both have already been consumed, while the band below spot is 65% long-side and has been GROWING. Spent short fuel above, live long fuel below. The participation test: open interest FELL 1.66% from $2,091,386,877.43 to $2,056,643,157.36 across the window in which price made and lost a new high, so contracts were closed, not opened - a squeeze completing rather than a trend starting. The positioning test: the long/short account ratio ROSE from 1.13 at midday to 1.22 on the 00:00Z bucket, the highest reading of the week, so the crowd that was fading the rally six hours ago is now long into a failed breakout. Funding agrees, having more than doubled from 0.00406% to 0.00912% per 8h - still small in absolute terms but now unambiguously longs paying shorts. Four independent measures, one direction. The nearest genuine magnet is 64,750 and the desk expects it to be tested before 65,000 is reclaimed.

divergences.note: The divergence the midday session flagged on the 15-minute frame has migrated up to the hourly and resolved as a rejection rather than a pause. Price made a higher high - 65,490.3 against the midday reference of 65,214.9, a 275.4-point extension that took out the 07 August and 31 July range tops - while the 1H MACD histogram collapsed from +41.03 to -13.60 and the line crossed beneath its signal. A new price high against a momentum reading that not only fell but changed sign is the strongest form of this signal, and on the hourly frame it carries considerably more weight than the 15-minute version the midday correctly treated as a size constraint. The midday's judgement was right on both counts: it named the 65,300 print as the momentum peak of the impulse rather than a launch point, and it declined to deploy the remaining 7.38 USDT on that basis. Price extended 190 points further than the midday's peak and then gave back 578. The signal is recorded here as the reason this session reduces rather than merely holds.

calibration.rollingRecord: 61 rows on file before this one. The 09 Aug midday session called range with a bullish tilt at 45/41/14 from 65,214.9, moved position to ADD, held the reduce at 64,650 for a tenth session, RAISED the add trigger from 65,000 to 65,300 with the open-interest condition attached, and deployed 5 of its 12.38 USDT of free cash into spot while explicitly keeping 7.38 dry. The scoring splits cleanly and it is worth splitting because the lesson is in the split. The DIRECTIONAL call was wrong: price is 64,912.3, down 302.6 points or 0.464% from the midday reference, and the 5 USDT tranche bought at 65,214.9 is worth 4.977, a loss of 0.023. Bullish tilt marked down. The RISK MANAGEMENT was right and was right for stated reasons. Holding 64,650 was correct for a tenth time - the lowest trade since is 64,838.7, so the line kept 188.7 points of clearance at its closest. Raising the add trigger to 65,300 WITH the open-interest condition is the decision of the day across all four sessions: price traded 190 points through 65,300 to 65,490.3, the trigger did not fire because the 22:00Z bar settled at 65,077.4 rather than closing above the level, and open interest fell 1.66% rather than rising, so both halves of the condition rejected a move that failed within the hour. Had the midday set a naked price trigger it would have bought the high of the week. And declining to deploy the full 12.38 - sizing 5 rather than 12.38 on the strength of a 15m bearish divergence it identified in advance - saved 7.38 USDT from being bought 300 points higher than it can be bought now. The midday seat carries the worst attributed record on the desk at -7.08 across fourteen decisions; today it made the single best call of the day and still lost 0.023 on the tranche it took. actingHelped is marked FALSE because the trade lost money, but the process that produced it was the strongest of the four sessions and should be repeated.

The rule the desk should carry into the overnight is the one that has now scored three times running: a level break is only worth acting on when open interest expands into it. It contracted 1.66% into this one.
